outcome: Incidence of postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV)
cohort: The study included 202 patients undergoing cesarean section at a tertiary care hospital.
finding: Spinal anesthesia for cesarean section was associated with better maternal postoperative outcomes, satisfaction, and early breastfeeding success, along with slightly better immediate neonatal adaptation, compared to general anesthesia.
mod_finding: Within the context of cesarean section, spinal anesthesia demonstrated advantages over general anesthesia for maternal postoperative outcomes, satisfaction, early breastfeeding success, and immediate neonatal adaptation.
